newsitem.title: USA: W.R. Grace to merge packaging unit with Sealed Air.
newsitem.headline: W.R. Grace to merge packaging unit with Sealed Air.

text.p: Package and chemicals firm W.R. Grace & Co. GRA.N said Thursday it would merge its packaging business with Sealed Air Corp. and create a new publicly-traded company.

In a joint news release, the companies said the transaction would be worth $5 billion in cash and stock in the new company to Grace shareholders. Grace said it also will spin off its specialty chemicals business to its shareholders.
The new publicly owned company, to be called Sealed Air, will be a global leader in protective and specialty packaging, with annual sales in excess of $2.5 billion, the companies said.
The transaction, tax-free to both companies and their shareholders, is expected to be completed in early 1998.
Grace shareholders will receive about 40.9 million common shares and 36 million new convertible preferred shares in the new Sealed Air.
On a fully diluted basis, Grace shareholders and current Sealed Air shareholders will own 63 percent and 37 percent, respectively, of the new Sealed Air.
Excluding the effect of transaction and integration costs, the deal is expected to be accretive to Sealed Air's earnings per share going forward.

Albert J. Costello, chairman, president and chief executive officer of Grace, will remain chairman, president and chief executive officer of the new Grace specialty chemicals company, and T.J. Dermot Dunphy, chairman and chief executive officer of Sealed Air, will be chairman and chief executive officer of the new Sealed Air.
The new company will consist of Grace Davison, Grace Construction Products and DAREX Container Products, have annual sales of about $1.5 billion and retain the Grace name.
Sealed Air is a global leader in protective and specialty packaging materials and systems.
